payload.goal: Make sofar measurably the best work memory for AI coding agents: never below any agent's native memory on any rep, bookkeeping at or below native overhead, and a lead of at least 25-30% (target 2x) on held-out long-horizon, cross-agent, decision-churn work. The lead must survive a native memory that syncs across machines and teammates, so it may never rest on native memory being machine-local.

phases.name: Phase 1 — Wave A: parity at native overhead (ships in 0.33.0-rc.2)

tasks.title: A1 overhead cut: adopt the session from CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (start_session becomes a fallback), load sofar MCP tools up front (no ToolSearch), a batched end_session taking decisions[]/tasks[]/notes[], task status derived from commits and tests instead of per-subtask update_task. PREDICT (chain A, prompt-matched pairs): store share ≤12% of tool calls on every rep; sofar/automemory cost ≤0.9; retention within ±1 decision. Contract Decisions first (SPEC start_session and end_session).

A2 rule fidelity: a rule stores the operator's quote beside it, the digest renders the quote, and a warning fires when a rule adds status codes, paths or values the quote lacks. PREDICT: claude-sofar S9 and A6 at 100% in 3 of 3 reps.

A3 digest composition: next task's spec first; remember entries surfaced; implementation minutiae dropped from rejected approaches and recent decisions; rules ranked by relevance and rendered last; ≤6k chars. PREDICT: ≤1 raw .sofar read per session; M3 unchanged or better.
rust-core mirrors 1.1–1.3 (hooks, digest render) with conformance parity before rc.2 is pinned

B1 read-time surfacing: when a file is read or edited, the decisions whose guard or derived scope matches it are shown, worded as facts (Claude PostToolUse on Read/Grep, Codex Bash/apply_patch, Cursor postToolUse). PREDICT: C3 re-violation −50%, tokens +<1%.

B2 repo-wide scope and supersession across initiatives: a rule can be app-wide; a reversal of a standing rule in ANY initiative is refused without supersedes (extends L08, which is same-record only). Fixes cursor-sofar's cross-record A2 loss.
B3 executable decision checks with fix hints in the failure, run at Stop, pre-commit and in drive. Blocking needs a Decision revisiting drift-hardening D3 (warn, never block) first.
B4 optional bridge into native memory (repo-local autoMemoryDirectory import, Codex summary), user/feedback types kept local. Needs a privacy Decision first.

payload.because: Round 1's only Claude quality miss was lost at capture. The operator said "Reject anything else"; the agent's rule added "with 4xx"; the "obey verbatim" header made that paraphrase law, so S9 returned 400 and failed A6. Keeping the operator's words beside the rule, and flagging what the rule adds in every digest, puts the source in front of each later session at zero extra calls. The write-time warning lets the capturing session correct the rule the moment it logs it. Frozen prediction: claude-sofar S9 and A6 at 100% in 3 of 3 reps.
payload.chose: 1.2 CONTRACT (rule fidelity). (a) decision_logged gains `quote?`: the operator's own words the rule came from, copied exactly, non-empty, at most 300 chars, valid only alongside `rule` (the guard pattern). (b) A pure core/rule-fidelity.ts lists a rule's SPECIFICS: HTTP status codes and classes (400, 4xx), paths (a token with `/` between word characters, or a file name with an extension), and values (backticked spans, double-quoted spans, tokens carrying a digit). It then reports the specifics the quote lacks, by case-insensitive whitespace-collapsed substring. (c) Standing constraints renders each quoted rule as `- [D<n>] <rule> — operator: "<quote>"`, plus ` (not in the operator's words: <specifics>)` when any are missing. The header becomes `Standing constraints — obey verbatim; where a rule quotes the operator, the quote decides (<N>):` ONLY when an in-force rule carries a quote, so quote-less records render byte-identically. decisions.md and the review packet render the quote too. (d) sofar_log_decision returns `warnings[]`, and `sofar event append --type decision_logged` prints them, naming the unquoted specifics; never a refusal. (e) The `rule` and `quote` descriptions and the CLI dialect's fields teach: word the rule as the operator did, and pass their words as quote. Guard notices in hooks are unchanged in 1.2.
payload.over: Refusing a rule that adds specifics (a paraphrase that rightly names a file would cost a retry, and the plan says warn); recording prompts so the quote can be verified mechanically (user content in the record); rendering the quote instead of the rule (the operator's sentence often lacks the context the rule supplies); clipping long quotes at render (a clipped quote can drop the clause that matters, so the cap sits at validation)

1.1 CONTRACT (overhead cut).
(a) ADOPTION: `sofar mcp` reads CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, which Claude Code ≥2.1.154 sets on stdio MCP servers (≥2.1.163 on resume). Before any tool except sofar_start_session runs with no active session, the server adopts that id exactly as sofar_start_session({tool: claude-code, session_id}) would: home beats branch, registration is idempotent, and a known id is pinned only. (b) ALWAYS-LOAD: tools/list marks sofar_end_session and sofar_log_decision with `_meta["anthropic/alwaysLoad"]: true` (memory-lead M1). The other seven stay deferred.
(c) BATCHED WRITE-BACK: sofar_end_session adds `decisions[]` (log_decision args minus initiative), `phases[]` ({phase, status, note?}, resolved like update_phase), `notes[]` and `memories[]` (strings). `tasks[]` entries gain `title` and `phase?`, which ADD a task the plan lacks (task_added). The whole batch is validated first: payloads, the D31 reversal check against the record plus the batch's earlier decisions, and phase resolution. One bad entry appends nothing and is named. Appends run in order (tasks, phases, decisions, memories, notes, session_ended) with ONE projection pass. The result names the new D/M handles and carries rule-fidelity warnings.
(d) The protocol block goes to V8, and SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS become per-process: with an adopted session there is no start_session step, and every write rides the write-back. sofar_log_decision is for mid-session use only when a concurrent session must see the decision first. The tool surface stays ≤8,000 chars.

payload.because: A record's decisions reach the agent once, at SessionStart, and only that record's. By the time a session acts on a file they are tens of thousands of tokens back (r1-fixes D16), and a rule from another record appears nowhere at all. record-index 3.2 pushes only GUARDED rules, 24 of the repo's 138, and only after the edit. Compliance decays within a session (arXiv 2605.10039: about 5.6% lower odds per generated function), so the fix is to re-surface at the point of use. A read is the first moment the path is known, and it comes before the edit. Measured on this repo (all initiatives): file tokens in chose, over and rule name 74 real files from 92 in-force decisions (30 ruled), median 1 decision per file, 8 files above 3. Directory tokens alone spread over 375 files, and adding `because` adds evidence mentions, not subjects. So the surface is precise and small, and told-once keeps a session's cost to a few hundred chars, which is where the tokens +<1% prediction comes from. The wording follows Claude Code's hook docs: text framed as out-of-band system commands can trigger prompt-injection defenses, so write factual statements. Today's guard notice is imperative.
payload.chose:
2.1 CONTRACT (read-time surfacing, B1).
(a) WHEN. PostToolUse also tests every path a call READS: Claude Code Read (tool_input.file_path) and Grep (tool_input.path when it names a file, plus tool_response.filenames when present, first 5); Cursor Read (file_path, else path; the live payload is checked before 2.1 is marked done); and on every host's shell call (Claude and Codex Bash, Cursor Shell) the operands that name an existing regular file inside the repo root, resolved against the hook's cwd, first 5, flags skipped. Edits keep their paths. Paths under .sofar/ or outside the root are never tested. Matchers: Claude PostToolUse becomes Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Bash|Read|Grep; Cursor postToolUse becomes Shell|Write|Read; Codex is unchanged. A read appends NOTHING to the record.
(b) WHAT. In-force decisions from EVERY initiative that either GUARD the path (a path: guard matches, as in record-index 3.2) or NAME it (a file token in chose, over or rule, using rule-fidelity's path class, that equals the path's tail at a / boundary). Directory tokens and `because` are not scope. In force mirrors the fold: a superseded decision is out (a ruled target falls only to a ruled superseder), and so is any until-scoped decision, since task resolution is not indexed. Edit-time guard notices stop asserting superseded rules too.
(c) ORDER AND CAP. Guards first (other initiatives before this one, as today), then ruled mentions, then unruled mentions. Within a tier, the longer matched tail wins, then the newest. Stored relevance (typed-judge D10) only reranks within a tier and adds; its reader lands with typed-judge 5.1. At most 3 decisions per call, then `…and N more decisions name <path> — sofar find <path>`. Rules render verbatim with the operator's quote (drift-hardening D2, memory-lead D2). chose and over render as heads cut at the first clause boundary, as the digest does (memory-lead D4).
(d) TOLD ONCE per (session, decision, path). The set lives in the derived index at .sofar/.index/told/<session>.json and is disposable: a lost file re-tells, never silences. Read and edit notices share it. SessionStart with source compact or clear empties it. The edit notice keeps its lastTouch suppression.
(e) WORDED AS FACTS. Guard: `sofar: <path> is governed by [<handle>], a standing rule: "<rule>" (guard: <guard>). Work against it needs a decision that supersedes <handle>.` Ruled mention: `sofar: [<handle>] names <path>. Its standing rule: "<rule>".` Unruled mention: `sofar: [<handle>] <date> names <path>: chose <head> over <head>.` record-index D2 holds: only a guard says "governed by". The edit notice takes the guard wording and drops "obey it verbatim".
(f) INDEX. guards.json becomes the decision-scope tier: per initiative, each decision with a guard or a file mention, carrying ordinal, ts, rule, quote, guard, heads, mention tokens and a superseded flag. INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION bumps. Still one refresh per hook call.
(g) No schema change, no new event type, no model call; warn-only (drift-hardening D3).
(h) Budget: ≤1,500 chars per call (rules are never clipped; the overflow line absorbs); Read-hook p50 within +5 ms of today's no-op Read (54 ms here, fast path).
(i) SPEC gets a §Read-time surfacing section and an acceptance entry; rust-core mirrors B1 as its own task.

2.3 CONTRACT (B3: executable decision checks), per the user's ruling relayed by sofar-c3 on 2026-09-22 ("Drive + opt-in pre-commit"). It QUALIFIES drift-hardening D3, which still governs guards.
(a) SCHEMA. decision_logged gains `check?: {cmd, hint?, timeout_ms?}`, valid only alongside `rule` (the guard pattern). cmd is a shell command, non-empty, ≤500 chars, exit 0 = the decision holds. hint (≤300) is the remediation shown on failure; absent, the rule and quote stand in. timeout_ms is 1..600,000. verification_recorded gains `decision?: "<slug> D<n>"`. Fingerprint re-emitted. The fold keeps DecisionState.check. A record with `decision` joins run.verifications (attempts count per task) and task.checks (latest per decision), and never overwrites task.verification, so the task's own verify pass keeps covering.
(b) TRUST. A check is agent-written text in a shared record, so it never runs unapproved. Approval is either the operator's `sofar check --approve <handle>` (TTY-confirmed, human-only; stores sha256(cmd) in a per-clone file under the sofar state dir, shared by worktrees, never committed or synced), or, in drive only, the run's surface covering it (commandAllowed, as r1-fixes D19). An applicable unapproved check is named with that command and never run. A changed cmd needs approval again.
(c) SCOPE. A check applies when its decision's path guard matches a changed path, or always when it has no path guard. Changed paths are the session's touched files (Stop), the staged files (pre-commit), files changed since the session's launch head (drive), and the working-tree changes (`sofar check`; `--all` runs every approved one). In force follows the scope tier: superseded checks never run. The check's cmd file tokens join the decision's mentions, so reading or editing the check's script surfaces the decision (ImpossibleBench: agents edit tests).
(d) WHERE, AND WHETHER IT BLOCKS. Failure line: `sofar: check for [<handle>] failed (<how>): <last line> — rule: "<rule>" — fix: <hint>`.
- Stop: checks run only when the write-back block already fires; failures ride its message and never cause a block. Total budget 45 s; per check min(timeout_ms, 30 s).
- pre-commit: a new never-clobbering git hook (the prepare-commit-msg precedent) runs `sofar check --staged`. It warns on stderr; exit 1 only when the operator opted in (`sofar check --block-commits on`, stored in the same per-clone file) and an approved check failed. Any internal error exits 0.
- drive: at task acceptance, after verify passes or when none applies, the applicable checks run. A covered pass (same cmd, same tree) runs nothing. A fail or timeout is recorded, reopens the task and files verify_failed with the line, and the next session's prompt gets it with the fix hint. A refused check is recorded and never blocks. Attempts share --max-verify-attempts.
- `sofar check` CLI: warns and exits 0 (`--strict`: 1 on a failure).
(e) Cursor, Codex and Claude share the Stop path, and git hooks are host-agnostic (r1-fixes D35). No model call. rust-core mirrors the schema, fold and scope-tier changes as its own task.

payload.because: D<n> is a position in ULID order. A union merge of two branches that both logged decisions, or a correction that voids one, shifts it. The fold then retires whatever now holds that position. The repro silently retired a teammate's standing rule and left the intended target in force beside its replacement. Event ids never move, and the writer knows the target at write time, so stamping the id there fixes every future supersession without changing what agents type.
payload.chose:
2.8 CONTRACT (merge-stable supersession, MOAT.md P0).
(a) SCHEMA: decision_logged and memory_promoted each gain optional `supersedes_id`, the event id (ULID) of the entry `supersedes` names. The writer stamps it and agents never pass it. It is valid only alongside `supersedes`. The fingerprint is re-emitted. Older readers ignore unknown top-level fields, so a pre-2.8 reader keeps today's ordinal behaviour.
(b) WRITER: ToolContext.appendAndProject (the only mutation path: MCP, batched write-back, CLI) stamps it from its own fold when the handle resolves: a decision at that ordinal in this record, or a memory in the named record. A handle that does not resolve (forward, self, unknown) stays unstamped and inert, as today. A caller-supplied supersedes_id that differs from the derived one is refused. Each batch append advances the fold, so a decision superseding an earlier one in the same batch gets that decision's real id.
(c) FOLD: a supersession carrying an id resolves by id among entries already folded, never by ordinal. An id that names no folded entry (voided, or absent) is inert. In state, `supersedes` becomes the resolved handle (D<current ordinal>), so projections name the decision actually replaced. Without an id, it resolves by ordinal, as before. Memories do the same within a record, and doctor's cross-record memory retirement resolves by id when present.
(d) SCOPE TIER: guards.json and labels.json apply the same rule. INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION bumps.
(e) OUT OF SCOPE:
- verification_recorded.decision. Coverage also needs the same command and tree fingerprint (driver/drive.ts), so a renumbered handle can only cause a re-run.
- Judge subjects (typed-judge).
- D<n> in prose and docs (note 01M341NV needs an operator ruling).
- Events logged before 2.8 keep ordinal resolution.
(f) rust-core mirrors this as 2.9.
PREDICT: the MOAT.md §4 repro ends with B's refund rule and A's per-entity rule in force and A's calendar-year rule retired. Every log without a merge-induced renumber folds and projects byte-identically.
payload.over: Accepting a ULID in `supersedes` itself: pre-2.8 validators reject a non-D<n> value and would drop the whole decision for older readers. A fold-only fix: the log records no branch lineage, so no ordinal rule can recover the intended target. Stamping in each writer (three copies instead of the one mutation path). Falling back to the ordinal when an id does not resolve (that ordinal is exactly what a merge moved). Including verification_recorded (safe-failing, and it widens the schema for no correctness gain).

payload.because: r1-fixes 3.3's line reads only this record's last 60 decisions and renders only `over`. It misses the cross-record re-proposals behind cursor-sofar's A2 loss, and every rejection older than 60 decisions. It also cannot surface a note, and notes are where most findings live on this repo (523 notes against 495 decisions). Precomputing terms turns per-prompt tokenizing into a lookup over postings. The `relevant` filter keeps the per-prompt write cost at zero on the common path, where only hooks' mechanical events arrived.
payload.chose:
3.1 CONTRACT (the prompt-time BM25 index), with the TypeScript reference first and rust-core mirroring it as 3.4.
(a) CORPUS: repo-wide. It covers every decision (chose + over + because, clipped to 1,200 chars) and every note (clipped to 1,200 chars) in every initiative, plus this record's stall handoffs as today. IDF runs over the whole corpus, retired entries included, so postings stay append-only. Retired entries are dropped only at render: own-record ones through retiredOrdinals(state), other records' through the tier's own supersession marks (stamped id first, memory-lead D12). Another record's until-scoped decisions are excluded outright, because whether their task resolved is not indexed.
(b) TIER: .sofar/.index/lexicon.json with meta-lexicon.json, maintained incrementally through passOverRecord, stamped with the existing INDEX_SCHEMA_VERSION and no bump (no existing shape changes). Per slug it holds a doc table (kind, ordinal, ts, token count, render heads clipped to 300 chars) and postings from term to flat [doc, tf, inOver]. Reducers gain an optional `relevant(event)`. A batch with no relevant event carries the state by reference and does not rewrite the file, so appending command_run never rewrites the tier.
(c) RENDER, at most 2 lines, with LESSON_MIN_TERMS, LESSON_MIN_SCORE, the young-record rule and the runner-up ratio unchanged. A decision whose matched terms occur in its `over` renders `sofar: ruled out before — [<h>] <over>`. Otherwise it renders `sofar: decided before — [<h>] chose <chose>`. A note renders `sofar: noted before — [<h>] <text>`. Every line ends in `(matched: …)`. <h> is D<n> for this record, `<slug> D<n>` for another, and `<slug> note <date>` for a note.
(d) TOLD ONCE per (session, doc) through core/told with the subject `prompt`. A lost set re-tells and never silences, and compact or clear empties it (memory-lead D6).
(e) FALLBACK AND ABLATION: an unreadable tier falls back to today's own-fold path (last 60 decisions). SOFAR_LESSONS=off disables the line, and SOFAR_LESSONS=fold forces the old path: the ablation arm that prices the index apart from r1-fixes 3.3 (r1-fixes D5).
PREDICT: C3 re-violation −30% relative to the fold-only line on Chain L's superseded and why-only probes, and cross-record re-proposals caught where the old line caught 0. Tokens +<1% (≤2 lines, told once). User-prompt p50 within D18's +10%. The rust-core lane measures that after the smokes (3.2/3.4). If it is over budget, the index defaults to `fold`.
payload.over: (1) Keeping the per-prompt tokenizing of the fold and raising the 60-decision cap: the cost is proportional to prose, about 90 ms at this repo's 1,100 docs. (2) Reusing reach.json: 1.6 MB parsed on every prompt. (3) Embeddings: they are barred without a Decision, and they cannot show which words carried a match. (4) Removing retired docs from postings: that breaks the append-only resume. (5) Two docs per decision, split into chose and over: a re-proposal phrased in the subject's words would no longer reach its rejection (the r1-fixes 3.3 finding). (6) Indexing memory entries now: they are already in the digest, and they would widen the scope past the task.

Session start fell 10,547 → 8,821 (rc.3 9,317) and undeferred per-prompt 14,191 → 8,030, as Wave A / L12–L13 predicted, but over a 10-prompt session the deferred total is ≈41k chars vs ≈12.6k on 0.32.0. Wave A1's overhead prediction held (store share of tool calls 7.7–10.6% vs round 1's 32–38%, R2-P8 ✓). cd ~/IO/handoff-bench/scenario5-launch-bench && python3 - <<'E'
p='PRE-REGISTRATION-R3.md'
s=open(p).read()
a="*Open risk for the operator:* at about 20 Codex sessions per window, the 48 Codex sessions take about three windows."
assert s.count(a)==1
s=s.replace(a,"At about 20 Codex sessions per window, the 48 Codex sessions take about three windows. **Reps-per-window ruling deferred to the first measured window** (operator, 2026-09-29, relayed by roadmap-h2): D32 stands; the real Codex sessions per plan window are measured from Oct 4, and reps are ruled on that number. No seat change and no rep cut now. **This does not block the freeze:** the freeze fixes arms, reps and predictions as drafted, and any later rep change is a logged deviation.")
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
cd .. && git commit -q -m "scenario5: R3 §9 CALENDAR — reps-per-window ruling deferred to the first measured Codex window (operator 2026-09-29); freeze fixes arms/reps/predictions as drafted, later rep changes are logged deviations; NOT frozen (memory-lead 5.3)" -- scenario5-launch-bench/PRE-REGISTRATION-R3.md && git log --oneline -1
